questions.question: What is the SQuAD dataset primarily used for benchmarking?
options: Extractive Question Answering (finding spans in a passage).
Detecting if a question is rude.
questions.explanation: SQuAD (Stanford Question Answering Dataset) is the gold standard for extractive QA, where the goal is to identify the start and end indices of an answer within a given context.

questions.question: In a RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) system, what are the two main components?
options: A retriever (finds relevant docs) and a reader/generator (produces the answer).
A tokenizer and an embedding model.
questions.explanation: RAG works in two stages: first, the retriever pulls relevant passages from a massive corpus; second, the reader (or LLM) processes those passages to answer the question.

questions.question: Why is 'refusal calibration' important in production QA?
options: It ensures the system says 'I don't know' when the answer isn't in the provided context, reducing hallucinations.
It prevents the system from answering questions in the wrong language.
It limits the number of questions a user can ask per hour.
It speeds up the retrieval process.
questions.explanation: If a system is forced to answer even when it lacks context, it will likely hallucinate. Proper calibration ensures the system admits its ignorance when necessary.

questions.question: What does the RAGAS framework measure in 2026 production QA?
options: Dimensions like faithfulness, relevance, and context precision without needing gold references.
The speed of the vector database.
The total number of tokens used by the LLM.
The accuracy of a model on the SQuAD test set.
questions.explanation: RAGAS provides reference-free metrics that allow developers to evaluate the performance of their RAG pipelines on real-world production traffic.
